title: Booking
description: Room reservations with authorization, time-aware cancellation, notifications through the outbox and durable state.
author: Codex and Claude · source-linked explanation
exclusions: Authentication of the real caller and truth of supplied time are external conditions.
Delivery timing and exactly-once notification processing are not established by these guarantees.
Migrated or externally modified database states are not automatically in the modeled reachable set.
The registry, dispatcher and Notifier are trusted and integration-tested; the kernel theorems stop at the destination ID.
Preservation of started bookings covers runs with nondecreasing time only, and admins may remove any booking.
Refusals are not stored under idempotency keys, and replies are rendered by a trusted mapping.

nodes.title: Bookings never overlap
nodes.description: Two distinct bookings of the same room share no instant, in any state reachable through accepted commands.

nodes.title: Valid bookings are accepted
nodes.description: A booking of an existing room, in the future, nonempty and apart from every booking of that room, is accepted and gets the next ID, as long as IDs are not exhausted.

nodes.title: Back-to-back bookings are both accepted
nodes.description: Intervals are half-open, so a booking that starts exactly when another ends is accepted. Without this, a service that refuses too much would still satisfy every safety guarantee.

nodes.title: Bookings follow the booking rules
nodes.description: Every booking a successful command writes is made by the caller, takes the next ID, names an existing room, starts after the engine's time, is nonempty and is apart from every existing booking of the room.

nodes.title: Only the owner before the start, or an admin, cancels
nodes.description: Every deletion a successful command writes removes an existing booking, and the caller is an admin or the booking's owner at a time before its start.

nodes.title: Permitted cancellations are accepted
nodes.description: In a reachable state, an admin's cancellation of any existing booking is accepted, and so is the owner's before the booking starts.

nodes.title: Started bookings remain
nodes.description: Once a commit has happened at or after a booking's start, later commands by non-admins cannot remove it, provided time never goes back between commits.

nodes.title: Only admins create rooms and appoint admins
nodes.description: A room is created only by an admin. An admin is added only by an existing admin, or by a caller adding themselves while there is no admin yet.

nodes.title: Notifications go to the room's destination
nodes.description: Every notification a successful command emits names the destination registered for its booking's room. Where that destination leads is decided by the operator's registry, outside the kernel.

nodes.title: Notifications describe the change they announce
nodes.description: A Booked notification is about a booking that did not exist before the command and exists after its writes; a Cancelled one is about a booking that existed and is gone.

nodes.title: Every booking and cancellation is announced
nodes.description: A write set that stores a booking also emits Booked for it, and one that deletes a booking also emits Cancelled for the deleted booking.

nodes.title: Reachable states keep the invariants
nodes.description: Unique keys, IDs below the counter, bookings of existing rooms, nonempty intervals and pairwise compatibility hold in the initial state and after every accepted command, at any time.

nodes.title: No command crashes the kernel
nodes.description: For every caller, state and command, the extracted transition returns a result: a write set and reply, or a refusal. No panic, arithmetic overflow or bad index is reachable in it.

nodes.title: Stored rows are what the specification computes
nodes.description: The kernel's apply computes the specification's applyAll, and in the store model the rows equal the encoding of that state; a load decodes to it up to row order.

nodes.title: Stored bookings keep the invariant
nodes.description: For the server's schema and any tenant, databases built from accepted write sets, interleaved with other tenants' statements, hold a state satisfying the invariant, and so does every snapshot a later load decodes.

nodes.title: No double booking
nodes.description: For a reachable state, any two bookings with different IDs and the same room share no instant t. The reachability hypothesis is part of its scope.

nodes.title: Apart means no shared instant
nodes.description: For nonempty intervals, Apart holds exactly when no instant lies in both. It turns the invariant's inequalities into the statement about instants.

nodes.title: Invariants in every reachable state
nodes.description: Induction over Reachable: init_inv for the empty service, inv_preserved for each accepted step.

nodes.title: Accepted commands keep the invariants
nodes.description: If the state before a successful transition satisfies Inv, so does the result of applying its writes. No hypothesis on the time.

nodes.title: What a successful command writes
nodes.description: Sums up the command lemmas in five cases: List writes nothing, AddAdmin, CreateRoom, Book and Cancel write the listed writes under the listed conditions. The later theorems split on these cases.

nodes.title: Every write is allowed by the policy
nodes.description: Each write of a successful command satisfies allowed, judged against the state before it, the caller's user and the time in the principal. Needs no invariant.

nodes.title: The kernel is total
nodes.description: For every principal, snapshot and command, transition returns ok with some result. Refusals are ok results carrying an error.

nodes.title: Notifications are sound
nodes.description: Assuming Inv on the state before, every emitted effect names the room's destination, Booked effects are about a booking new in the result, and Cancelled effects about one that is removed.

nodes.title: Changes come with their notification
nodes.description: Every PutBooking in a successful write set has a Booked effect for that booking, and every DelBooking has a Cancelled effect for a booking with that ID.

nodes.title: Acceptance of a valid booking
nodes.description: Requires an existing room, a start after the principal's time, a nonempty interval, apartness from every booking of the room, and a counter below the maximum. Then Book returns Created with the next ID. The declared touching-interval mutant is relevant to this acceptance boundary; actual failure attribution requires a run.

nodes.title: Acceptance of a permitted cancellation
nodes.description: In a reachable state, for an existing booking, an admin or the owner before the start gets Done. Reachability supplies the booking's room through the invariant.

nodes.title: Availability check is exact
nodes.description: free returns true exactly when the interval is apart from every booking of the room. The equivalence matters: the direction that free accepts every compatible interval is what acceptance relies on.

nodes.title: Scenario: touching booking accepted
nodes.description: On the extracted code, with [1, 2) booked in room 0, a booking of [2, 3) by user 3 at time 0 returns Created 2 with the booking, counter and Booked notification to destination 7.

nodes.title: Scenario: owner cancels before the start
nodes.description: On the extracted code, user 2 cancels booking 1 ([1, 2)) at time 0 and room 0's destination 7 receives the Cancelled notification.

nodes.title: Preservation after start
nodes.description: Requires a timed reachable state, a run with nondecreasing time restricted to non-admin callers, membership of the booking, and a start no later than the time of the latest commit.

nodes.title: apply computes applyAll
nodes.description: The kernel's generated apply yields a snapshot whose list view is Spec.applyAll of the write set, as long as no vector can overflow.

nodes.title: The store holds what apply computes
nodes.description: For a database served through the modeled store, it holds the encoding of the state, and a load that lists the tables decodes to an equivalent state up to row order.

nodes.title: Invariant on stored state
nodes.description: For valid schema and tenant inputs, PgServed histories of accepted write sets imply Inv, and every decoded load satisfies Inv. Required by the manifest's check.

nodes.title: Clock reversal permits cancellation
nodes.description: An owner cancels at time 0 after a commit at time 5, removing a booking that started at time 1. Every step is accepted; only the last goes back in time, which StepsT excludes. This is a formal counterexample to dropping monotonic time.

nodes.title: Overlapping booking is refused
nodes.description: With [1, 2) booked, a request for [1, 3) in the same room returns Taken. Acceptance does not extend to intervals that share an instant with an existing booking.

nodes.title: Booking in the past is refused
nodes.description: At time 5, a request for [5, 6) returns InThePast: a start equal to the engine's time is not in the future.

nodes.title: A stranger cannot cancel
nodes.description: User 3, not an admin, cancels user 2's booking and gets Forbidden.

nodes.title: The owner cannot cancel after the start
nodes.description: User 2 cancels booking [1, 2) at time 1 and gets Started. The owner's right to cancel ends at the start, judged by the principal's time.

nodes.title: Half-open intervals
nodes.description: Intervals [start, end) can touch without overlapping. Different rooms are compatible; bookings of the same room must be apart.

nodes.title: Booking invariant
nodes.description: Unique keys, fresh IDs, existing rooms, nonempty intervals and pairwise compatibility.

nodes.title: The policy
nodes.description: allowed says which writes a user may make in a state at a time: admins, rooms, bookings, deletions, the counter, and where an effect may go.

nodes.title: Meaning of a write set
nodes.description: applyWrite upserts admins, rooms and bookings, filters out a deleted booking and sets the counter; Emit changes no table. applyAll folds it over a write set.

nodes.title: A room's registered destination
nodes.description: destOf is the destination ID stored on the room, if the room exists. It is a number; the registry maps it to an endpoint.

nodes.title: Rows of a state
nodes.description: enc lists the admins, rooms, bookings and counter as table rows; sqlA gives each write's table operation, and none for Emit.

nodes.title: Accepted write sets
nodes.description: Write sets the kernel returns for some principal and command it accepts, at any time. db_inv quantifies over histories of these.

nodes.title: Reachable state
nodes.description: The state comes from the empty initial state by accepted transitions. Arbitrarily corrupted or migrated states are not automatically reachable.

nodes.title: Time never goes backwards
nodes.description: ReachableT and StepsT model nondecreasing time. Applying this theorem to the running service relies on the engine's clock contract.

nodes.title: A run by non-admins
nodes.description: StepsT with the filter that the caller is not an admin in the state of each step. Admins may remove started bookings by design.

sources.anchor: (h : StepsT (fun a st => ¬ isAdmin st a.user.val) st t st' t') {b : Booking}

nodes.title: IDs not exhausted
nodes.description: book_accepted assumes the counter is below U64.max. At the maximum, Book is refused with Overflow instead.

nodes.title: No vector overflow
nodes.description: apply_spec assumes the snapshot's rows plus the write set's length stay below the usize maximum, since each write adds at most one row.

nodes.title: Server schema and tenant value
nodes.description: db_inv assumes a valid table list with the kernel's key lengths, four tables, and a tenant value of integer kind.

nodes.title: Database & engine contract
nodes.description: Relies on modeled PostgreSQL semantics, serializable transactions, faithful value conversion, tenant consistency and restricted database credentials.
excludes: Live deployment conformance is not established by a Lean build.

nodes.title: Authenticated caller & clock
nodes.description: The shell supplies the actor and the engine stamps the time. Theorems over these values do not establish that an external identity or clock is truthful.

nodes.title: Bearer token authentication
nodes.description: HmacAuth verifies the token and passes its organization and user to principal. The key, its storage and the expiry clock are trusted.
excludes: Who holds a valid token is outside the proofs.

nodes.title: Database clock, monotonic
nodes.description: config selects the database's transaction time with monotonic on, so servers of one database agree and commit times never decrease per tenant. Nothing checks that the clock is right.
excludes: A clock that is ahead or behind still decides what counts as the future.

nodes.title: JSON command and reply codec
nodes.description: Decodes the request body into a Command with unknown fields denied, so the client cannot send a time. Encodes replies and maps refusals to HTTP statuses. The mapping is trusted.

nodes.title: Extraction and the Lean checker
nodes.description: The theorems are about the Lean that Charon and Aeneas produce from the kernel, starting at transition. Faithful translation and a sound checker are assumed; extraction freshness is a separate check.

nodes.title: Notification delivery
nodes.description: The operator's registry maps destination IDs to endpoints; the dispatcher delivers at least once with a stable key. Order across retries, deduplication by receivers and unknown destinations are outside the kernel theorems.

nodes.title: POST /rpc
nodes.description: The framework's rpc_router: authenticates the caller, decodes the JSON command and runs it through the engine, honoring Idempotency-Key.

nodes.title: Engine
nodes.description: Per attempt: one SERIALIZABLE transaction that loads the tenant, reads the time, stamps it, calls transition and commits the writes. Retries reload and read a new time.

nodes.title: Rust transition
nodes.description: Dispatches AddAdmin, CreateRoom, Book, Cancel and List into write sets and replies, or a refusal.

nodes.title: Rust booking checks
nodes.description: Checks the room, interval, current time, availability and ID bound, then emits the booking, counter and notification writes.

nodes.title: Rust availability check
nodes.description: Scans the bookings for one of the same room with start_at < end and start < end_at. The touching-interval mutant changes these comparisons.

nodes.title: Rust cancellation
nodes.description: Finds the booking, lets an admin through, otherwise requires the owner and a time before the start, then deletes it and emits Cancelled to the room's destination.

nodes.title: Rust admin and room commands
nodes.description: add_admin accepts an admin or the bootstrap case; create_room requires an admin and takes the next ID.

nodes.title: Rust write dispatch
nodes.description: apply_write puts or deletes rows and sets the counter; Emit changes nothing. schema! builds apply from it.

nodes.title: Rust table writes
nodes.description: sql_write gives each write its table operation through the generated schema; an effect has none.

nodes.title: Commit & load
nodes.description: The server's Store uses generated schema loads and compiled SQL writes. Effects go to the outbox.

nodes.title: Outbox enqueue
nodes.description: Store::write inserts each Emit into the outbox in the request's transaction, so a notification exists exactly when its change commits. The payload omits the destination.

nodes.title: Dispatcher and Notifier
nodes.description: A loop sends committed outbox rows once a second. Notifier logs or POSTs each delivery with its Idempotency-Key and a timeout.

nodes.title: PostgreSQL agreement test
nodes.description: Runs random commands with a forward clock through PostgreSQL and the in-memory engine and compares replies, states and outbox rows. Skipped without a test database.

nodes.title: Clock reversal test
nodes.description: Replays the clock_back_cancels run on PostgreSQL: without monotonic the owner's cancellation succeeds, with it the kernel answers Started.

nodes.title: Outbox delivery tests
nodes.description: Checks posting to the room's endpoint, no notification for refusals, retry with the same key, and that an unregistered destination is never contacted.
